faqs.question: How much proof of funds for Hungary or Poland student visa?
faqs.answer: Enough to cover remaining tuition plus living costs for the period the mission asks. Amounts change — verify the current checklist. SK Immigration reviews bank statements case by case; round “magic numbers” from social media are unreliable.

faqs.answer: Germany uses Sperrkonto/blocked account rules often. Hungary and Poland usually use bank statements, sponsor letters or other living-cost proof listed by the mission — confirm the current guide for your intake.

body:
Answer: Show enough money for remaining tuition + living costs for the period your mission lists. Numbers change by year and city — do not trust fixed Facebook screenshots. SK Immigration Services (SK Consultant) reviews statements case by case before you book VFS.

What “proof of funds” usually means

  • Student / sponsor bank statements with a clear trail
  • Tuition payment receipts or scholarship letters
  • Sometimes a sponsor affidavit + relationship proof
  • Living-cost coverage matching housing plans

Hungary vs Poland — practical notes for Pakistan

Both are popular budget Europe options. Living costs and tuition vary by university and city. SK maps your offer letter to the current embassy/VFS checklist rather than quoting a single viral number.

  • Hungary study visa Pakistan
  • Poland study visa Pakistan
  • Cost calculator · Compare countries

Germany is different

If someone told you “blocked account for Hungary,” they may be mixing Germany’s Sperrkonto rules. See blocked account Germany and Germany study visa.

Red flags SK rejects

  • Sudden large deposits with no explanation
  • Borrowed balances returned after biometrics
  • Statements that do not match the sponsor story

  2. Share offer letter + last 6 months statements (redact as needed)
  3. Get a written checklist before you pay authority fees

Walk-in: Satellite Town Rawalpindi. Verify CUIN 0304985 on /about/.

Attestation still matters

Funds proof does not replace document attestation. Sequence stamps with document services so your educational papers match what Hungary or Poland missions expect for your intake.
